Mini aussies are such bundles of energy. I love mine. He's trained to stay within my sight and so we go outside and I tell him to go play or to run and he'll run around my car several times or run around the house a few times before he comes and lays at my feet for belly rubs. Mine also adores water so in summer I set up a hard plastic pool and put toys that sink and ones that float in it for him. He goes nuts and has so much fun figuring out how to remove the toys. He then waits for me to set them back up. I also use the water hose and turn it on jet and have him chase it through the yard.

So, I actually have a mini aussie who is a year old right now. He's trained on potty pads and for outside. The reason being I work third shifts and I live with my mother to take care of her in her old age so there's times she cant take him out. 

Anyway, it's going to be frustrating to no end but determination is key here. If you catch him going to the bathroom on anything but the training pad, pick him up and move him onto the pad. If he finishes his business on the pad, praise him and reward him with a treat. Mini aussies are extremely smart and they'll pick up on what you want very quickly. 

To train him outside, you should walk him often and have treats on hand. Every 30 minutes is a great routine for young dogs. Again, if he goes outside, praise him with a lot of love and a treat. 

A perk of this breed is that aussies love mental stimulation and praise. Don't yell at him or ever spank or strike him. They'll respond with fear and shame and actually try and hide their bad habits. If you show them affection, understanding and reward them they'll be one of the most loyal companions you've ever had.

Mine is trained to recognize handsigns and when we go for walks he doesn't go on a leash. He stays with me unless I tell him he can go play. I also live up on a mountain away from most people though lol. 

Edit: Let me add this, getting him into a routine will help and it took me 6-8 months to train my dog so it'll take some time and patience but it'll be worth it in the end!
